post.description:
Uploads a PDF (multipart/form-data, field `file`) and queues it for reading. Returns 202 with the document in status QUEUED; poll `GET …/documents/{document_id}` for progress. The file is checked for size, PDF signature, structure, encryption and page count before anything is stored. It is kept privately under a server-generated name, and the client's filename is only a label. Extracted content is only ever a draft: it reaches the exam's questions through POST …/approve and nowhere else.

Errors: `EXAM_NOT_DRAFT` (409), `DOCUMENT_ALREADY_UPLOADED` (409, `errors[0].error` is the existing document id), `TOO_MANY_DOCUMENTS` (409), `PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE` (413), `UNSUPPORTED_MEDIA_TYPE` (415), `INVALID_PDF` (422; `errors[0].error` is NOT_A_PDF, MALFORMED, ENCRYPTED, TOO_MANY_PAGES or NO_PAGES), `EXTRACTION_UNAVAILABLE`, `QUEUE_UNAVAILABLE`, `STORAGE_UNAVAILABLE`, `BUSY` (503). Rate limited per user.

post.description:
The one and only way extracted content reaches the exam. Copies the reviewed draft into the exam's questions, after the ones already there, in one transaction: all of it or none of it. The exam must still be a draft; it is locked for the duration, so it cannot be published half-way. Publishing and assigning are not done here: use the exam's own publish endpoint afterwards. Approval needs a complete draft: marks set on every question, at least two options on every multiple-choice question, every diagram described and confirmed, and every blocking warning acknowledged. All problems are returned together as 409 `DRAFT_INCOMPLETE` with `errors[].field` such as `questions[2].points`. Each question's text is composed from its instructions, the question, its tables (as rows of text) and its confirmed diagram descriptions, because that single text is what a candidate hears.

Errors: `VALIDATION_ERROR` (400), `DRAFT_INCOMPLETE`, `STALE_VERSION`, `ALREADY_APPROVED`, `EXAM_NOT_DRAFT`, `INVALID_STATE`, `CONCURRENT_CHANGE` (409).
